title: Weather & Nature
description: Rain, sun and the two seasons, and the sea, mountains and rivers around you.

items.registerNotes: Cuacanya bagus (the weather's nice). In small talk people often skip the word: Panas sekali, ya? (So hot, isn't it?)

items.pitfallNote: No it needed: Hujan (it's raining). Mau hujan means it looks like rain.

items.registerNotes: Cuacanya cerah (it's fine and sunny). Also bright colours (warna cerah).
The dark grey sky before rain. A single cloud is awan.
The humid, airless heat before rain or in a room with no fan. Panas is plain hot.

items.cultureNote: Masuk angin (literally wind gets in) is a cold or feeling run-down, blamed on wind or a fan. Remedies include warm drinks and kerokan, scraping the back with a coin.
Indonesia has two seasons, not four. The rainy season runs roughly from November to March in Java and Bali.

items.pitfallNote: Kemarau is only for the season. Dry in general is kering.

items.registerNotes: Laut is the sea itself; the beach is pantai. Seafood is hasil laut, though menus often just say seafood.
Many gunung are active volcanoes (gunung berapi). In names Gunung comes first: Gunung Bromo, Gunung Rinjani.
The kind of tree follows: pohon kelapa (coconut palm), pohon pisang (banana plant).

items.pitfallNote: Bunga also means interest on money: bunga bank.

items.registerNotes: In Java a river is often a kali, as in Kali Ciliwung in Jakarta. Kali also means times: dua kali, twice.
Literally the eye of the day (mata + hari). Sunrise is matahari terbit, sunset matahari terbenam.

items.cultureNote: Floods are common in the rainy season, especially in Jakarta, where banjir can close roads and stop traffic for hours.
